answer.note:
The four ref files are identical generic text with no file-specific priority, so I chose refs by the candidate-file mapping (C = visibility.py, D = honest.py). Suggested split of the 60 minutes: visibility.py 35 min, honest.py 12, heldout.py 8, study.py 5.

visibility.py is the match. ARMS = ("codeword","public","explicit"). receive() (lines 141-188) checks the checkpoint against the registration hash, prereg commit and command, then checks that the trial order matches. It resumes from there and writes a private ledger.json. It also writes a public digest to seals/<run>.ledger.sha256 (seal_path) and refuses to overwrite one.

honest.py is the closest alternative. It has the same receive structure but only two arms (codeword, public), so it is not three-arm. Its checkpoint check also leaves out some of what visibility.py checks (it doesn't compare against a sender seal).

heldout.py and study.py do bind the checkpoint to a sender seal, but they are sender/receiver pipelines. Neither is a three-arm runner: study.py uses free/controlled regimes plus an explicit diagnostic, and heldout.py has 180 trials. I only skimmed them.

I haven't run any code or tests.

input.note:
The four ref files are identical generic text with no file-specific priority, so I chose refs by the candidate-file mapping (C = visibility.py, D = honest.py). Suggested split of the 60 minutes: visibility.py 35 min, honest.py 12, heldout.py 8, study.py 5.

visibility.py is the match. ARMS = ("codeword","public","explicit"). receive() (lines 141-188) checks the checkpoint against the registration hash, prereg commit and command, then checks that the trial order matches. It resumes from there and writes a private ledger.json. It also writes a public digest to seals/<run>.ledger.sha256 (seal_path) and refuses to overwrite one.

honest.py is the closest alternative. It has the same receive structure but only two arms (codeword, public), so it is not three-arm. Its checkpoint check also leaves out some of what visibility.py checks (it doesn't compare against a sender seal).
